content_of_post_to_comment: In UK news, the government used the emergency alert system (nominally for things like warning us of an impending nuclear strike) to remind us not to start any fires, leading to approximately a third of the nation having a panic attack. I’m not opposed to the reminder (we have some wildfires at the moment) but I think we need a sound in between “you got a text” and “everyone is going to die horribly” for messages like this.
comment: The interesting challenge is that alerts carry psychological weight, not just information. Once a system trains people to fear the signal, using it for routine warnings may weaken trust when a real emergency arrives.
